subject.title: [Bug]: macOS app 'Launch at login' stops sticking / appears to turn itself off after app updates

question: Should the macOS app persist OpenClaw-owned Launch at login intent and re-register the app LaunchAgent after startup/update drift, or should live launchd/System Settings state remain authoritative?
rationale: Current code treats live launchd state as authoritative, while the report asks for enabled user intent to survive app replacement; changing that behavior can either restore user intent or accidentally override deliberate external disables.

options.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
options.body: Store explicit in-app enabled intent and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after startup or update drift, with guards for deliberate external disables.

options.title: Keep launchd authoritative
options.body: Leave live launchd/System Settings state as the toggle source and document that OpenClaw will not restore externally disabled login items.

options.title: Wait for packaged update proof
options.body: Keep this parked until a current-main Sparkle update reproduction identifies exactly which state flips.

recommendation.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
recommendation.body: Store explicit in-app enabled intent and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after startup or update drift, with guards for deliberate external disables.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for Launch at Login persistence and macOS app ownership decisions points to steipete through PR 607 and the OpenClaw macOS app rename/config work.
